title: Field Trip Vote
story: Your class is choosing a field trip. Every student writes the code of one destination on a slip: 4 for the aquarium, 9 for the science museum, 17 for the climbing wall, and so on. The slips go into a box and are read out one by one.
The school rule says a trip only goes ahead if one destination gets more than half of all votes. This time the teacher already knows it happened. You just need to say which destination won.
task: Write winningTrip(votes). Return the destination code that appears more than votes.length / 2 times.
Such a destination always exists, so there is always exactly one correct answer.
constraints: One value appears more than votes.length / 2 times.

examples.explanation: Five votes, so the winner needs at least 3. The museum, code 9, got 3. The aquarium and the climbing wall got one each.
Seven votes, so the winner needs at least 4. Code 17 got exactly 4. The first vote read out was a 4, but that does not make it the winner.

hints: With 7 votes, how many does the winner need? Once some destination reaches that number, could anything still beat it?
You need to know how many votes each destination has so far. A tally sheet with one line per destination is enough.
Which structure keeps a count per destination code, with no idea in advance which codes will show up?
Walk the votes once with a map from code to count. After adding each vote, check whether that count is now more than votes.length / 2. If it is, return that code right away.
bruteForce: For each vote, scan the whole box and count how many slips match it. Return the first code whose count is more than half.

Every vote can trigger a full scan, so this is O(n²). With 50,000 votes that is up to 2.5 billion comparisons. Sorting also works, because the winner must fill the middle position, but it costs O(n log n) and reorders the slips.

js: * @param {number[]} votes  one destination code per student
* @return {number} the code with more than half the votes

tests.note: winner not first in a row
alternating, winner never twice in a row
first vote is not the winner
winner only appears in the second half
winner bunched at the start, one vote at the end
last vote and middle slip (unsorted) are both losers

js: const count = new Map(); // destination -> votes so far
if (c > votes.length / 2) return v; // nobody can catch up now
return -1; // never reached: a winner always exists
py: if count[v] > len(votes) / 2:  # nobody can catch up now
return -1  # never reached: a winner always exists
walkthrough: Read the slips once and keep a running tally per destination, like marks on a whiteboard. The moment one destination passes half the class, it has won.
Trace [9, 4, 9, 17, 9]. Half of 5 is 2.5, so the winner needs 3.
• 9: tally 9 → 3, which is more than 2.5. Return 9.
Use the total number of votes in the check, not the number read so far. After the first slip, that one destination has 100% of the votes read, but it has not won anything.

There is also a neat O(1) memory trick: keep one candidate and a counter, add 1 when a vote matches the candidate, subtract 1 when it does not, and switch candidate when the counter hits 0. Each losing vote cancels one winning vote, and the winner has more votes than everyone else combined, so it is the one left standing.
solution.timeWhy: One pass, with O(1) average work per vote for the map update.
solution.spaceWhy: The map holds one entry per different destination, up to about n / 2 of them.
solution.takeaway: To find which value occurs most, or past some threshold, keep a hash map of counts while you walk the list. It replaces one full recount per element with a single update.
